sn12.66:1.7: _Sammasa_ is an unusual term in the suttas. The root is _mas_, to touch or rub. I’m reminded of the medical idea of self-examination, touching or rubbing your body to see if there’s a lump or pain.
sn12.66:3.6: “Attachment” is _upadhi_, which is both the things of the world to which we cling, and the inner clinging (see [snp1.2](), [mn105:28.2.]()). The Jains defined _upadhi_ similarly (Tattvārthasūtra 9.26). The dominant meaning in Sanskrit is “fraud”, which perhaps informs the Buddhist sense: the things we attach to give a false sense of security. Here it plays the role of “grasping” (_upādāna_).
sn12.66:13.10: “Seasoned drink” is _bhaṭṭhaloṇikā_, “fried salty”. Perhaps a drink seasoned with fried or parched spices and salt. | “Broth” is _loṇasovīraka_, a fermented bean paste used for broth, comparable to miso. | Read _ahitāya dukkhāya_, following PTS and Bodhi.
